text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said in Laos there were several worthwhile projects on which Singapore and Malaysia could work to their mutual benefit and it was time to move on after the recent diplomatic row between the two countries.
- Singapore has stopped the import of all pork and pork products from Taiwan because of the recent outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease there.
- Singapore once again is the world's second most competitive economy behind the United States, the Swiss-based International Institute for Management Development said.
- Aztech Systems said it managed a turnaround in the second half of last year with a Singapore $5.0 million gain.
- There were apparent attempts to ramp up the price of Singapore Telecom shares, brokers claimed.
- SingTel is taking a wait-and-see attitude on the paging market and will only make a decision whether to cut prices by June or Juny.

- Singapore property tycoon Ng Teng Fong paid a staggering HK$11.83m billion for a piece of waterfront residential land in Hong Kong, giving the territory a vote of confidence three months before it returns to Chinese rule.
- Competition in the paging market is heating up and is set to drive prices of services down by more than 20 percent.
- Wall Street managed to stay firm, rising by 20.77 points by noon, ahead of expectations the Federal Reserve Board would raise interest rates.
- United Industry Corporation and its subsidiary Singapore Land chalked up small rises in group net earnings for 1996.
- Sembawang Maritime Ltd defied market expectations with an impressive jump in group net profit for 1996 of 81 percent to S$16.59 million.
- Diversified United Engineers Ltd reported a lower than expected 54 percent increase in net profit to Singapore $15.05 million last year with only its property business shining out.
